newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - February 4.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - February 4.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, the Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends ***********************************************
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

PARIS - Prospects are raised of transforming France's media landscape when French conglomerate Generale des Eaux and Havas say they are discussing their interests in audiovisual activities, primarily pay-television Canal Plus. Shares in Havas Advertising rise strongly on rumours that Havas wants to increase its stake in the 39 percent-owned unit.

HERZOGENAURACH, Germany - German sportswear maker Adidas hires French advertising group Publicis as its partner for worldwide World Cup 1998 public relations. Adidas says the international programme will continue through the 1998 World Cup in France and will be managed from Paris by Idees Dialogue Conseil, the public relations unit of Publicis.

LONDON - Institute of Practioners in Advertising complains to British government about fast-rising cost of TV advertising space and says state-funded BBC is being allowed to compete unfairly in "ratings battle" with commercial channels.

LONDON - Commercial radio stations claim a record 4.9 percent of Britain's total advertising market from July to September 1996, says the Radio Advertising Bureau. Commercial radio's previous greatest share of the UK advertising market had been July to September 1995, when it claimed 4.7 percent.

PARIS - France is expected to authorise the marketing of genetically-modified maize as early as this week after drafting its own compulsory labelling code. France initially said it would approve the sale of genetically-modified maize only when the European Union labelling rules were in place. But France said that if the EU did not move fast enough it would come up with its own labelling rules.
LONDON - Ammirati Puris Lintas Spain, a unit of Interpublic Group of Cos Inc, names Philippe Bernard chairman. Bernard succeeds Manolo Ramilo, who recently retired.
MEDIA AND THE INTERNET:
MOUNTAIN VIEW, Calif. - Excite Inc, which runs Internet search and navigation services, launches what it says will be the first free news clipping service available over the World Wide Web.

AMSTERDAM - Europe's network of internet companies is set to consolidate over the next 18 months, with smaller service providers being swallowed up by telecoms firms and larger providers, says the Yankee Group telecoms consultancy.
TOKYO - Japanese-language Internet service provider Yahoo! Japan Corp says it plans to list its shares on Japan's over-the-counter market, buoyed by a surge in Japanese Internet users.
SYDNEY - Global media group News Corp must report a sharply higher second quarter profit on Thursday or it will fail to achieve its 20 percent growth target for the 1996/97 year, analysts say.

PANAMA CITY - Panamanian consortium Medcom Holding Inc says it has bought Panama's main cable television company, Cable Onda 90, for $32 million. Cable Onda 90 has 25,000 subscribers. Medcom already holds the country's two main television channels, RPC Television and Telemetro.
HANOI - Hanoi said on Friday it would step up internal vigilance and increase domestic propaganda in response to plans by U.S. radio station Radio Free Asia to begin broadcasts to Vietnam.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS AND MARKETS:

JOHANNESBURG - U.S. soft drinks giant Coca-Cola is to invest $60 million in the next three years in Zimbabwe as part of plans to expand its business throughout Africa. The company has already announced that it will increase investment in South Africa.

WARSAW- PepsiCo's restaurant unit plans to increase its number of outlets in Poland from 49 to 170 in the next three to five years, the company says. It has already invested $57 million in Poland since 1993, with employment, currently at 3,000, likely to rise to 10,000 in three to five years.

LONDON - British mobile phone firm Vodafone Group says it will expand its presence in Greece by acquiring another five percent shareholding in Panafon SA, a local cellular network operator and a similar stake in Panavox, a service provider to Panafon.

NEW YORK- Fashion designer, Tommy Hilfiger, plans to open his first international flagship store in London during 1998. The company says it expects the store to create exposure in Britain and boost the brand across Europe.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

NEW YORK - For teenage girls, "grunge" is a thing of the past and its once again "cool" to be dressed up, which is good news for some teen-oriented retailers. The rekindled passion for fashion has breathed new life into the whole teenage fashion market, say industry sources.

LONDON - Sales of personal computers in Europe lost momentum in 1996, pulled back by stodgy German sales and by customers waiting for the new MMX technology, according to an industry research company, Context. Western Europe's PC sales rose a healthy 11.5 percent in 1996 to 16.4 million, it says.

BEIJING - China's Public Security Ministry is issuing a record number of passports to people travelling abroad at their own expense after it loosened restrictions on overseas trips, says Xinhua news agency. Some 2.4 million people went abroad at private expense last year. The number of people going to Hong Kong and Macau fell last year, but travellers to Taiwan, which Beijing regards as a renegade province, soared by 20 percent to 51,000.

SINGAPORE - A software piracy watchdog, the Business Software Alliance, plans to fight rising CD-ROM piracy in Singapore by targeting end-users and pushing companies to join a new corporate programme to guard against huge losses in revenue. Software theft by piracy in Asia exceeded US$4.3 billion in 1994 -- about 29 percent of the US$15.2 billion lost worldwide.
MIAMI - Lawyers pressing a Florida class-action suit against cigarette makers begin a three-month publicity campaign to notify Florida smokers and their survivors of their legal rights.

PARIS - French customs say seizures of counterfeit goods at Orly, the Paris airport, in the first nine months of 1996 rose sharply against the same period the previous year. Clothing and clothing accessories acounted for 34 percent of counterfeit goods seized followed by automotive parts, watches, CDs and perfume.
